claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has favorable plasticity and machinability.
Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low hardness and strength.
The combination of favorable plasticity and machinability with low hardness and strength is governed by the absence of nanoscale precipitates or ordering.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi alloy is a homogeneous, disordered, single-phase solid solution with minimal secondary precipitates.
The absence of secondary phases permits relatively easy or unhindered dislocation glide in the starting alloy.
Easy dislocation motion produces reduced strength and hardness while preserving high ductility.
An aging heat treatment can induce nanoscale precipitates or local ordering in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The controlled comparison is between as-cast and aged samples of the same equimolar CoCrFeNiTi composition.
Mechanical testing is to be conducted under tensile and compressive loading from 25 °C to 600 °C.
Aging-induced nanoscale precipitates will act as barriers to dislocation motion.
The proposed strengthening contribution from the precipitates is Orowan strengthening.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, the aged alloy will contain discernible nanoscale precipitates.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, the aged alloy will have increased hardness.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, the aged alloy will have increased compressive strength.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, the aged alloy will have reduced ductility.
In multiphase or substantially compositionally deviated CoCrFeNiTi alloys, strengthening mechanisms other than the proposed precipitate-absence mechanism could dominate.
The aging temperature and time required to reproducibly induce an optimal precipitate population without excessive ductility loss are not determined.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant strength and hardness increase with a corresponding ductility decrease is proposed as a falsifying result.
Failure of the aging treatment to produce nanoscale precipitates is proposed as a falsifying result.
